# csv-rfc4180

A CSV parser, streaming parser and serializer for Node.js (18 or later). It has no dependencies and is a single CommonJS file, `src/csv.js`.

```js
const { parse, createParser, stringify, CsvError } = require('csv-rfc4180');

parse('name,age\r\nAda,36\r\n');
// [['name', 'age'], ['Ada', '36']]

parse('name,age\nAda,36\n', { header: true });
// [{ name: 'Ada', age: '36' }]

stringify([['a,b', 'say "hi"'], ['']]);
// '"a,b","say ""hi"""\r\n""\r\n'
```

## `parse(text, options)`

Returns an array of records. Each record is an array of strings, or an object keyed by column name when `header` is true.

| Option | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `delimiter` | `','` | One UTF-16 code unit other than `"`, CR and LF. |
| `header` | `false` | Use the first record as column names. |
| `skipEmptyLines` | `false` | Drop lines with no characters at all. |

- Records end at CRLF, LF or CR. A single line break at the end of the input does not start another record.
- An empty line is the record `['']`. A line containing only `""` or a space is not empty, so `skipEmptyLines` keeps it.
- A field is quoted only if its first character is `"`. Inside quotes, `""` is one `"`, and delimiters and line breaks are data. In an unquoted field, `"` is an ordinary character.
- Fields are never trimmed.
- A byte order mark at the very start of the input is dropped, and does not count toward column numbers.
- In header mode, duplicate column names and records whose field count differs from the header are errors. A header with no records gives `[]`. Records are plain objects; a `__proto__` column becomes an ordinary own key.

Unknown option keys are ignored, so one options object can go to both `parse` and `stringify`.

### Errors

Arguments of the wrong type throw `TypeError`. Malformed input throws `CsvError`, which has 1-based `line` and `column` properties. Lines are counted at every CR, LF or CRLF, including those inside quoted fields, and columns count UTF-16 code units.

| Problem | Reported position |
| --- | --- |
| Quoted field never closed | its opening `"` |
| Character after a closing `"` that is not a delimiter or line break | that character |
| Duplicate header name | start of the second occurrence |
| Wrong field count (header mode) | line where the record starts, column 1 |

If the input has several problems, the first one met reading left to right is thrown. A duplicate header name is found when its field ends; a field count is checked when its record ends.

## `createParser(options)`

A streaming parser that takes the same options as `parse`.

```js
const parser = createParser({ header: true });
parser.write('id,na');       // []
parser.write('me\r\n1,Ada\r'); // [{ id: '1', name: 'Ada' }]
parser.write('\n2,Alan');    // []
parser.end();                // [{ id: '2', name: 'Alan' }]
```

`write(chunk)` returns the records whose ending line break is in `chunk`. `end()` returns the final record if the input does not end with a line break. Chunks can split the input anywhere, including inside a CRLF, a quoted field or a `""`. The records and errors are always the same as `parse` returns for the whole input. After `end()` or after any throw, both methods throw a plain `Error`.

The parser keeps only the current field and record, so memory and time grow with the size of the input, not with the number of chunks.

## `stringify(rows, options)`

| Option | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `delimiter` | `','` | Same rules as `parse`. |
| `eol` | `'\r\n'` | `'\r\n'` or `'\n'`. Written after every record, including the last. |
| `header` | none | Array of column names, written first. Rows may then be objects. |

- Strings are written as they are, numbers and booleans with `String()`, and `null` and `undefined` as empty fields. Other types throw `TypeError`.
- A field is quoted when it contains the delimiter, `"`, CR or LF, or starts or ends with a space. Each `"` inside is doubled.
- A record whose only field is empty, whether from `''`, `null` or `undefined`, is written as `""`. Otherwise it would be an empty line, which `skipEmptyLines` drops.
- When the output would start with U+FEFF, the first field is quoted, because `parse` drops a leading BOM.
- With `header`, object rows are written in header order. A missing key, meaning one that is not an own property, is an empty field. Array rows are still written as they are. With no rows, the output is the header line alone. `header: false` or `null` means no header.
- With no header and no rows the result is `''`. A row with no fields becomes an empty line.

`parse(stringify(rows, options), options)` returns `rows` for any rows that are non-empty arrays of strings, with or without `skipEmptyLines`.

## Tests

```sh
npm test
```

- Unquoted fields lose spaces and tabs at both ends.

- If the delimiter is a space or tab, it stays a delimiter under `trim`.
